content.text:
```yaml
- id: DR-01
  requirement: >
    The service must let a fleet technician add a new drone to their own
    company's fleet.
- id: DR-02
  requirement: >
    The service must let a fleet technician retire a drone from their own
    company's fleet. Once a drone is retired, the service must not allow it
    to be assigned to any flight.
- id: DR-03
  requirement: >
    The service must let a fleet technician take a drone out of service for
    repairs. While a drone is out of service, the service must not allow it
    to be assigned to a flight or signed off for a flight.
- id: DR-04
  requirement: >
    The service must let a fleet technician put a drone that was out of
    service for repairs back into service. After that, the drone can again
    be assigned to flights.
- id: DR-05
  requirement: >
    The service must let a fleet technician set up charging pads at their
    own company's sites. Each company has a few dozen pads, and each pad
    belongs to the company that set it up.
- id: DR-06
  requirement: >
    The service must let a fleet technician send one of their company's
    drones to charge at one of that same company's charging pads. It must
    not allow a drone to be sent to another company's pad.
- id: DR-07
  requirement: >
    For each drone, the service must keep a lasting record of every one of
    these events, with the date, the time and the person who did it. The
    events are adding the drone to the fleet, taking it out of service for
    repairs, putting it back into service, sending it to charge, and
    retiring it.
- id: DR-08
  requirement: >
    When regulators ask, the service must let a company produce the full
    record of how a given drone of its own has been looked after. This must
    also work for drones that have since been retired.
- id: DR-09
  requirement: >
    The service must not let a user from one company see or change another
    company's drones, charging pads, sites, flights, jobs or problems.
- id: DR-10
  requirement: >
    The service must not show the platform's airspace desk any individual
    company's fleet, jobs, sites, flights or problems.
- id: DR-11
  requirement: >
    The service must let a dispatcher plan a flight by choosing which of
    their company's drones flies it and which way it flies through the
    corridor network.
- id: DR-12
  requirement: >
    The service must not let a flight leave until a licensed dispatcher has
    signed it off. It must record which dispatcher signed off each flight as
    the person responsible for it.
- id: DR-13
  requirement: >
    The service must not accept a dispatcher's sign-off for a flight whose
    way passes through either of the following during the planned flight
    time. The first is a zone where the authorities prohibit flying. The
    second is a closure that is in force at that time.
- id: DR-14
  requirement: >
    The service must let a dispatcher call off a flight, both before it
    leaves and while it is in the air.
- id: DR-15
  requirement: >
    The service must not allow the same drone to be assigned to two flights
    that overlap in time. This applies even when several dispatchers are
    planning at the same moment.
- id: DR-16
  requirement: >
    When two dispatchers try at the same moment to assign the same drone to
    overlapping flights, the service must accept only one assignment. It
    must tell the other dispatcher that the drone is already taken.
- id: DR-17
  requirement: >
    When two dispatchers change the same flight plan at the same time, the
    service must not let one dispatcher's change silently overwrite the
    other's.
- id: DR-18
  requirement: >
    The service must keep one shared picture of the airspace that is the
    same for every company. This picture holds the network of flight
    corridors between sites, the zones that group those corridors, the
    zones where the authorities prohibit flying, and the closures announced
    by the authorities.
- id: DR-19
  requirement: >
    The service must let the airspace desk maintain the network of flight
    corridors between sites and the zones that group them.
- id: DR-20
  requirement: >
    The service must let the airspace desk enter a planned closure with a
    start time and an end time. The service must treat that closure as in
    force only between those times.
- id: DR-21
  requirement: >
    The service must let the airspace desk enter a sudden closure. The
    service must treat it as in force from the moment it is entered.
- id: DR-22
  requirement: >
    The service must let the airspace desk amend a closure that has already
    been entered, including widening its area and moving its end time. The
    amended closure must apply to all companies from the moment the
    amendment is saved.
- id: DR-23
  requirement: >
    When a closure is entered or amended and it affects flights already in
    the air, the service must at once alert the responsible dispatcher of
    each affected flight. This applies to every company that has such a
    flight.
- id: DR-24
  requirement: >
    When a closure is entered or amended and it affects flights that are
    planned or signed off but have not yet left, the service must flag
    those flights to their dispatchers.
- id: DR-25
  requirement: >
    When a closure is entered or amended, the service must show the airspace
    desk how much disruption it caused across customers. It must show this
    only as totals across all companies and never in a form that reveals
    any single company's flights or jobs. What counts as disruption still
    needs to be agreed with the airspace desk, because the interview did not
    define it.
- id: DR-26
  requirement: >
    The service must update the disruption totals shown to the airspace
    desk whenever the closure they relate to is amended.
- id: DR-27
  requirement: >
    The service must place each drone report according to the time the
    drone made it, not the time it arrived. A report that arrives late must
    never replace a newer report already received for the same drone.
- id: DR-28
  requirement: >
    When the same drone report arrives more than once, the service must
    count it only once.
- id: DR-29
  requirement: >
    For every drone in the air, the service must show its dispatcher the
    time of the last report received. It must flag the drone when no report
    has arrived within a set time. The length of that time still needs to
    be agreed with the dispatchers.
- id: DR-30
  requirement: >
    When a drone restarts in flight after a software fault and carries on,
    the service must treat its later reports as part of the same flight.
    It must not treat them as a new flight or as a different drone.
- id: DR-31
  requirement: >
    During a flight, the service must compare the battery level the drone
    reports with the level planned for that point. It must alert the
    dispatcher when the reported level is lower than planned.
- id: DR-32
  requirement: >
    The service must not lose any closure, amendment, sign-off, call-off or
    fleet change that it confirmed as saved. This applies when the service
    is updated, restarted or crashes.
- id: DR-33
  requirement: >
    After an update, restart or crash, the service must be working again
    within a few minutes, as the companies accept. The exact limit still
    needs to be confirmed with the companies.
- id: DR-34
  requirement: >
    When the service comes back after an interruption, it must treat as in
    force every closure whose time came while it was down. It must
    immediately send the dispatcher alerts and flags for affected flights
    that it would have sent during that time.
- id: DR-35
  requirement: >
    When the service comes back after an interruption, it must accept and
    correctly place drone reports made while it was down, including reports
    that arrive late or out of order.
```
